texts: Like the tree that bows to the wind and the spinning wheel that turns at a hand's touch, the student learns by yielding
my grandmother sat me down under the big tree by her spinning wheel and told me to first stop talking and just listen, if I wanted to learn her craft
student, tree, spinning wheel
doha pls on a student who is ready to be taught, tree and spinning wheel

Write a doha about a humble pupil who sits under a tree beside a spinning wheel and empties his mind of pride, ready to receive whatever the master offers, since only the humble can be filled with true learning
I want a doha for the student who knows he knows nothing, who bows without argument and listens without arguing back, and who therefore receives what a proud and clever person never could receive
Lay down your pride before the master, and he will raise you; lay down your cleverness, and he will fill you
an obedient pupil
my new coach asked me to forget everything I thought I knew about the game and start again from scratch, and that was the day I finally improved
doha on being a good student, surrendering ur ego before ur teacher
doha on a student who is open like a lotus and ready to learn
my little niece sat on the pond's edge watching a lotus open, and for the first time she listened to her teacher without interrupting once
Can you shape a verse about a student whose heart is like a lotus, opening slowly to the master's word, free of pride and full of readiness, blooming for the one who waits with patience and surrender
The lotus opens only when morning breaks; so the pupil's heart opens only when it is ready and bowed
lotus, humble student

Looking for a doha about a pupil who crosses miles of sand to reach his teacher, asks for nothing but a place to sit, and follows each instruction with his whole heart, since readiness is what makes teaching possible
I walked barefoot over the hot sand to reach my teacher's place, and that was the first lesson in how much I wanted to learn
doha on a student who goes through anything for learning, hot sand and all
sand, eager student
Over the burning sand the student goes with bare feet and an open heart, for the thirst to learn is greater than the pain
At the ringing of the bell the student sets down his sword of ego, and arrives empty so that he may be filled
doha for a student who obeys the bell and drops the sword of his ego
Give me a doha on the pupil who comes at the sound of the bell, lays down the sword of his pride at his teacher's feet, and listens in silence, ready to be filled with learning
my martial arts master rang a bell to call us and made us leave our swords at the entrance, and he said nobody can learn with a closed mind
bell, sword, obedient student
Write a doha about a pupil who sits before a cleric with folded hands and a quiet mind, not arguing, not boasting, ready to take in what he hears, because the humble mind is the one that receives
doha on a student who respects the cleric and listens without arguing
my cousin studied under a cleric who told him to drop his arguments at the entrance, and he did, and learned more in a year than in five
cleric, humble student
The cleric speaks and the pupil listens with a bowed head, and in that bowing something sacred enters
Drain the cup of knowing and the teacher will pour; hold it full and he will only watch it overflow
unlearn first, then learn
I want a doha about the student who empties himself of everything he thinks he knows and arrives with a quiet heart, so that whatever the teacher says can find room to settle and grow inside him
I went to my first dance class sure I knew everything, and my teacher told me to sit out until I could stand there with nothing but willingness
doha on a pupil who is ready to unlearn everything
surrender of the student
my father told me when I started at the workshop that the first month I should only watch and carry things and say nothing
doha on a student who obeys the teacher fully

Can you shape a verse about a student's full surrender to a master, the kind that does not question each instruction or seek a reason for each task, but simply trusts, and in that trust receives the entire lesson
Surrender is the first lesson and the last; only the one who bows can be lifted
doha pls on the student's humility
my son wanted to argue with every correction at his chess academy, until his coach asked him to simply do as told for one month, and now he is a champion
He came to the master empty-handed and empty-minded, and so he left filled with all there is
empty to be filled
I would like a doha about the student's readiness, that a student must come with an empty mind and a willing heart, so that the teacher's word may find a place in him and not slide off proud walls
student, one-string lute
doha for a student with a one-string lute who is ready to learn
my little nephew puts down his tablet and sits quietly before his teacher and the one-string lute, ready to listen, and I keep thinking how few adults can do that
He plucks the one-string lute only when the master nods, and out of obedience a music no pride could play begins

Write a doha for the pupil who sits before his master with a one-string lute, plucking only when told, learning each note by listening first, because he knows that surrender to the master precedes real skill
ready to receive
doha on a student who listens and learns without ego
when I got into my first real job, my boss said the best employees are the ones who admit they know nothing, and I remembered it every day
The empty mind is a clear sky, and the master's word falls into it like the first rain

Give me a doha on the pupil who understands that the teacher cannot fill a mind that is already full, and who therefore comes with empty hands and a willing spirit, asking for nothing but the chance to learn
Where pride stands tall the teaching slides off; where the head is bowed it sinks in and takes root
doha on why humble students learn most

Write me a doha about the student whose humility makes him ready for teaching, who respects his master, takes correction gladly, and so moves forward while the proud and clever remain stuck where they began
my brother was always the cleverest in class but he never really learned until he failed once and agreed to listen
humility opens learning
touchstone, river, humble student
doha on a student with a touchstone mind and a river of patience

I need a doha about a pupil who tests himself on the touchstone of obedience and sits like a river bank, receiving the teacher's flowing word without resistance, since the surrendered student learns and the rest merely listen
every day my teacher made me wash my work in the river and test it against the touchstone before submitting, and I never argued, and I became a better craftsman
The student is the river's bed and the master the rain; the touchstone is his readiness to be filled and tested
Can you shape a verse about the pupil who steps into the boat and gives the oar to his master, trusting his words even when a snake of doubt hisses in his ear, since surrender is the only way across
boat, snake, trusting student
my grandfather learned to be a sailor by simply obeying his master, who warned him about every snake in the grass and every current under the boat
The boat obeys the helm, the student his master; let a snake of doubt bite and the voyage is lost
doha on a student who trusts the teacher like a boat trusts its steersman, snake too
my cousin had run in circles for years like a musk deer chasing a scent he was carrying himself, until he stopped, sat before his teacher, and opened his cage of opinions
cage, musk deer, student
Compose a doha about a student who is like a musk deer chasing the scent that comes from himself, and who opens the cage of his pride only after he sits humbly before a teacher and learns to listen
doha on a student ready to leave the cage of ego, with a musk deer
The musk deer searches far for the scent in his own navel; so the student must stop, and let the master show him the open cage within
clay, potter, student
Give me a doha on the pupil who is like soft clay in the potter's hands, who does not stiffen or resist, but lets his master shape him gently until he becomes a vessel ready to hold the truth
doha on a student being shaped by a teacher like clay by a potter
at my pottery class my teacher told me to stop resisting the wheel and let the clay centre itself, and I realised it was true of learning too
The clay does not argue with the potter's hands, and so becomes a vessel; the student likewise yields and is formed
cotton, chakor bird, student
my aunt spun cotton in her village, taught by a patient old woman, and she watched that woman like a chakor bird for a month without a single question
doha on a student as soft as cotton and focused as a chakor bird
Write a doha about a student with a heart soft as cotton, ready to be spun into whatever the master wishes, and a gaze fixed on his teacher as the chakor bird's gaze is fixed upward
The chakor bird gazes upward without turning and the cotton lets itself be spun; so the student waits on the master
Make room, O student, and the master will fill it; keep none, and he will give you all
when my daughter started the new school she told me she was going to listen more than she talked, and I hoped she would keep it
surrendered learner
doha on how real learners drop their ego

I want a doha about the student whose pride has no room in the presence of his master, who sits low, speaks little, and obeys fully, because he understands that learning comes only to the one who first makes room
The seed that waits in dark ground grows tall, and the pupil who waits grows deep as the ocean, if he does not resist the master's soil
seed, ocean, surrendered student

Can you shape a verse about the student who is like a seed buried in the earth, surrendering fully to the teacher's patient watering, until what was a small thing in the dark grows large as the ocean in depth
doha on a student as a seed and the teacher as the ocean, surrender
when I first saw the ocean my teacher dropped a seed in my palm and said stop thinking how large it is, just plant it and wait, and that is how I learned to learn
I used to chatter all day in the market where I worked until my mentor asked me to hold my tongue for a week and just listen to people, and I learnt more than ever before
The market roars with a thousand tongues, but the student holds his own and listens, and so hears the master
doha on a student with a quiet tongue in the market of noise

Looking for a doha about the student who holds his tongue in the noisy market of opinions, learning to listen before he speaks, ready to receive his master's guidance, since the one who talks cannot learn
tongue, market, silent student
I came to my master like a beggar, hoping only for a few scraps of wisdom, and he gave me the philosopher's stone of attention, which was more than I deserved

Give me a doha on the student who comes to the master like a beggar before a philosopher's stone, empty-handed and pleading, knowing he has nothing, and so being transformed by what the master touches him with
The beggar asks the philosopher's stone for nothing but to be changed, and in his emptiness is turned to treasure
doha on a student who comes like a beggar to the philosopher's stone, empty and ready
beggar, philosopher's stone, student

Compose a doha about the pupil who obeys his master's instruction even when he does not understand it, because he trusts that the master sees further, and in that trust finds that understanding arrives by itself
doha on a student ready to obey his teacher no matter what
His will is laid down at the master's feet, and what rises from there is not his own, yet more his own than ever
my sister gave up her phone for three months at her teacher's request, and says she has never learned so much in her life
obedient student's surrender
doha on a student who is humble like a needle, thin and willing
I learned embroidery from an old woman who let me do nothing but pass a needle through scrap fabric for a whole month, and I never grumbled once
A needle passes through cloth only when it is thin and sharp; so the student passes through the master's teaching by being small

Can you shape a verse about the student who makes himself small and sharp like a needle, passing through the toughest teaching without a bulge of pride, since only the humble can be sewn into the master's wisdom
needle, humble student

Compose a doha about the pupil who puts his trust in the teacher the way a blind man trusts his guide, asking nothing and following each instruction, since surrender is the pupil's only sight on the unfamiliar road
The blind man puts his hand in the guide's and walks; so the student, seeing nothing, trusts, and arrives
blind man, trusting student
doha on a student who trusts his teacher like a blind man trusts his guide
my uncle, a blind man now, had to learn everything again from a young helper, and he listens to him with more humility than he ever did when he could see
When the student is ready, the teacher appears; when the heart is quiet, the word is heard
I want a doha about readiness, that moment when a student stops making excuses and arguing, sits quietly and surrenders to the teaching, so that all the master has to give can finally enter him
I almost left my music academy twice, but both times something told me to stay silent and keep practising, and now the lessons are finally sinking in
ready student, waiting teacher
doha on the student who is ready to learn
The heron stands still on one leg for its catch; the student stands still before the master, and a pearl is born
doha on a student, a pearl and a heron, patient and humble
Give me a doha on a pupil who waits like a heron, still and silent, for the pearl of understanding to rise from the master's words, and does not rush or fidget or argue but simply stays ready
pearl, heron, patient student
I watched a heron stand motionless at the pond for an hour, and my teacher said that is how a student should wait for a pearl of understanding
cloth sheet, surrendered student
my mother spread a cloth sheet on the floor and told my brother to sit before the tutor and listen, no questions for the first hour
He spreads himself like a cloth sheet at the master's feet, and what falls upon it stays
doha on a student who spreads himself like a cloth sheet before the teacher

I need a doha about the student who lays himself like a clean cloth sheet before his teacher, spotless, ready, and without a single stain of pride, so that whatever colour the master chooses will take
my uncle's teacher put him to work at the churn for months without teaching, and he was like sand drinking rain, ready for anything when finally a word came
Can you shape a verse about the student who is like dry sand that takes in every drop, and the churn that turns patiently again and again, so he learns by yielding daily to the master's instruction
The sand receives the rain and the churn gives butter; the student who yields to the master gives the world his best
doha on a student who is like sand receiving rain, and a churn
sand, churn, student

Compose a doha on the ideal pupil, who arrives free of conclusions, who is willing to be corrected without sulking, and who sits at his teacher's feet with a mind as open as a field waiting for the first rain
a surrendered mind
doha pls on a good pupil with no ego
Fold your hands and quiet your mind; the master's word needs no force, only a room
my friend's boy has been taking lessons for eight years and what impresses me is that he still asks every question as if it were his first
my potter uncle's apprentice rubs sandalwood paste on his hands each morning before kneading clay, and says the teacher is the only one he never questions
potter and clay, sandalwood, student
Sandalwood gives its scent to the axe that cuts it, and the clay yields to the potter; so the student gives himself and is made
Give me a doha on a student who gives himself to his teacher like clay to the potter and sandalwood to the axe, resisting nothing and offering fragrance, since the surrendered pupil is made whole
doha on a student with sandalwood and potter and clay, giving himself to his master
thief, grindstone, patient student
my grandfather said the grindstone of discipline his master put him through made him lose the thief of laziness within, and he never complained

Compose a doha about the student who bears the grindstone of hard discipline without complaint, so that the thief of ego who steals learning from the proud cannot touch him, and he becomes what the master wished
doha on a student, thief of ego and a grindstone of practice
The grindstone wears the blade smooth and the thief of ego steals away; the student bears the grinding and shines
churn, patient student
doha on a student who lets the teacher turn him like a churn, patient
The churn turns round and round, and the pupil is turned with it, until the butter of understanding rises
every evening my mother made me sit at her churn and listen to her stories; I learned patience without ever being told that was the lesson

Can you shape a verse about the pupil who lets the master churn him, again and again, without complaint, until what is light and precious rises to the surface and the heavier part of his ego settles at the bottom
doha on a student, not just a parrot but a moth that gives himself up
The parrot repeats the word, the moth gives up its wings; the student who wants to truly learn gives all

Looking for a doha about the true pupil who is neither a parrot repeating the master's word without meaning, nor a distracted moth, but one who surrenders fully and takes the teaching into his whole being
my little cousin repeats like a parrot whatever his tutor says, but the real student is the one who listens like a moth that gives up all for the burning
moth, parrot, devoted student
student, sun, readiness
Give me a doha on a student who rises before the sun each day to sit in humility before the teacher, eager to learn, asking for nothing, and ready to follow whatever instructions are given
doha on a student who comes to learn before the sun is up
The sun asks nothing of the field, and the field asks only to be open; so the student waits for the master's word
every morning before the sun was up, my son sat before his violin teacher and refused to look at his phone, and now he plays beautifully
my brother quit his job and moved to another city to study under one particular master, and told us he would not return until the master released him
doha on a disciple who surrenders to the teacher completely
total surrender
What the pupil gave away in surrender returned as a freedom he had never known

Write a doha on the willing student, who accepts the master's correction like a gift, never taking it as an insult, because he knows his own eyes cannot see his own faults and he needs another to show him
my father's old student sat by him through every night in the last weeks, carrying the shroud of his teacher's final request without complaint
At the shroud's edge the loyal student bows and finds in service the last lesson his teacher had to give
doha on a student who obeys the teacher till the very end, shroud too
Can you shape a verse about a loyal pupil who attends his master to the final hour, takes up the shroud and the last instruction with equal care, and learns in that surrender what no book could teach
loyal student, shroud
The lotus opens petal by petal under the master's gaze, never pulled, never forced, only waiting and receiving
doha on a pupil who opens like a lotus to the teacher, patient
my niece sat by the village pond watching a lotus open, and her teacher whispered that a good pupil opens the same way, with no force
lotus, receptive student

Write a doha about the student who opens like a lotus to the teacher's word, a petal at a time, never rushed and never closed, and in the quiet receptiveness of his heart finds all the learning he sought
I need a doha about the student who understands that the first duty is to listen, to hold back the quick answer, to let the master's words settle like grains in good soil, and only then to act
The ears of the student are the master's entrance; open them wide, and let silence be your pride
listening is learning
doha pls on a student who listens carefully to his teacher
my daughter used to interrupt every explanation but this year she has learned to wait, and her teacher says her listening is what changed her
doha on a student who does the chores before getting lessons
He swept the floor for a year and was richer by it than the one who learned in an hour but grasped nothing
student's trust
a boy came to our village asking to learn from the old craftsman in the lane, and sat three months doing only chores before he was given any lesson

Give me a doha on the student who patiently does the humblest work for his master before any lesson is given, sweeping, carrying, and waiting, since service is the soil in which the real teaching grows
I followed my mentor around his workshop like his shadow for a whole year before he trusted me with a single tool, and I would not trade that year for anything
As the shadow walks wherever its body walks, so the pupil walks wherever the master leads, asking nothing
student, shadow, obedience
doha on the student who follows his teacher like a shadow

I need a doha about the student who follows his master like a shadow, always near, always listening, and learns more by his silent presence than a hundred loud pupils could by asking a hundred questions
the blind man who sells flowers near our school walks perfectly with his young guide, trusting every step, and our teacher told us students should trust that way
doha on a blind man who follows his guide, like a student

Compose a doha for a student who puts his trust in his master like a blind man putting his hand on his guide's shoulder, asking no questions about where the road goes, and who arrives safely because of it
blind man, trusting pupil
The blind man follows a child's hand without fear; so the student walks with the master through the dark
my master asked me to find a needle in the desert sand, and I searched for days without a word, and that was the lesson
needle, sand, humble student
In the desert sand the pupil finds the needle of humility, and the master's hand shows him how to hold it

Compose a doha for the student who, asked to find a needle in the sand, does not argue about how impossible it seems but searches patiently, because obedience is the only road to what the master wishes to teach
doha on a student who searches for a needle in the sand when the teacher says so
At the cremation ground the pupil lays down his pride, and the diamond of the master's word shines in its place
diamond, cremation ground, student
Write a doha for the pupil who goes with his master to the cremation ground and surrenders all his plans there, ready to be filled with the diamond of insight that only the humble can receive
my teacher once took me to the cremation ground by the canal and told me to sit till I had no opinions left, and when I stood up I held a diamond of silence
doha on a student, a diamond and the cremation ground, learning from the end
doha on a student who learns from the teacher even without words
Be a student of the master's silence and of his speech, for both are the same source
my son has started to watch his teacher's hands closely instead of asking why, and I think he is finally learning

Write a doha for the pupil who learns even from his master's silence, who watches each gesture and holds each pause as a lesson, and who knows that sometimes a teacher teaches most when he says nothing at all
silent learner
an open student
my father began learning classical singing at sixty and says the hardest part was admitting to his much younger teacher that he knew nothing
doha on being a good student, humble and ready
Come to the master as the thirsty come to the stream, with nothing in the hands and everything in the heart
I'd like a doha about the grace of an open student, neither proud of what he knows nor afraid of what he does not, who sits easily before his master and asks to be taught, the beginning of wisdom
my grandfather taught me to use a winnowing fan, and I rubbed sandalwood on his forehead after each lesson, and he said that is how a pupil learns

Can you shape a verse about a student who is like a winnowing fan, letting the husk of his pride blow away in the master's presence, and like sandalwood, offering his fragrance to his teacher without being asked
sandalwood, winnowing fan, student
doha on a student with a winnowing fan and sandalwood
The student is the winnowing fan that lets the husk of ego blow away, and sandalwood that gives its scent to the master
The lion of the proud heart bows before the master's gaze, and in that bowing the pupil is truly born
I used to be the loudest boy in class like a lion, but my teacher stared at me quietly until I lowered my head, and since then I have started to learn
lion of ego, student
Looking for a doha about the student who comes to his master with a roaring lion of pride and sits quietly until the lion lies down, since only a tamed ego can learn what the teacher has come to give
doha on a student who tames the lion of ego for the teacher

Give me a doha on the pupil who keeps a calm tongue before his master, who answers when asked and listens when told, understanding that the one who speaks too much has less room for what he came to receive
my teacher once told me that I spoke too much, and held up a finger to my tongue, and from that day I started to really listen
doha on a student who holds his tongue to listen to the teacher
silent tongue, listening student
Still the tongue, and the master's voice will begin; quiet the mind, and his silence will teach
chakor bird, student
doha on a student who watches the teacher like a chakor bird watches the sky

Please write a doha about the student whose eyes never leave his master, like the chakor bird that never takes its eyes from the sky, devoted completely and learning by watching and obeying, with no thought for anything else
The chakor bird gazes only upward, the student only at the master; their love is their learning
my apprentice sits and watches me work for hours the way a chakor bird watches the sky, and I can see how much he is learning from simply being devoted
my aunt gave her son a cotton shirt and told him to go to the cleric's class with the same softness, to listen like the cloth and learn
doha for a student soft as cotton, learning from a cleric
Soft as cotton the student waits before the cleric, ready to be spun and woven into truth
cotton, cleric, student
Write a doha about a student with a heart soft as cotton who sits at the feet of the cleric, listening with humility and trust, so that whatever the cleric says may be spun into the cloth of his life
